ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is similar to $\triangle DEF$ with point O as the center of similarity. If $OD=3OA$ and the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $4$, what is the area of $\triangle DEF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$ are similar,\\
thus $AC\parallel DF$,\\
thus $\triangle OAC\sim \triangle ODF$,\\
thus $\frac{AC}{DF}=\frac{OA}{OD}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
thus $\frac{{S}_{\triangle ABC}}{{S}_{\triangle DEF}}={(\frac{AC}{DF})}^{2}=\frac{1}{9}$,\\
since ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=4$,\\
therefore ${S}_{\triangle DEF}=\boxed{36}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached geometry diagram shows point O on the left. From O, dashed rays go outward to the larger triangle on the right, with the smaller triangle ABC closer to O and the larger triangle DEF farther from O. The corresponding vertices lie on the same rays from O: A is on the ray toward D, B is on the ray toward E, and C is on the ray toward F, matching the stated center-of-similarity structure. Reasoning: Since O is the center of similarity and OD = 3OA, the dilation ratio from triangle ABC to triangle DEF is 3. Areas of similar figures scale by the square of the linear scale factor, so the area scale factor is 3^2 = 9. The area of triangle ABC is 4, so the area of triangle DEF is 4 × 9 = 36.
